# Editor sessions and PIE

Behavior observed in this project's UE 5.8 editor sessions on the primary workstation. Read it before launching an editor for MCP work, running scripted PIE sessions or captures, or measuring cost. The authoring workflow is in [Unreal MCP asset authoring](unreal-mcp-asset-authoring.md). Correct this file in the same PR when a finding no longer holds.

## Launch an editor

- A new worktree needs three steps before the editor opens:
  1. `git lfs pull`. Content files are otherwise 129-byte pointers, and the editor fails fatally in `URpgAssetManager::GetGameData`.
  2. The NetworkPrediction/Mover overrides: `prepare.py check`, `stage`, and `verify` with `--engine`, as `Build/Patches/NetworkPrediction/README.md` describes.
  3. `python Build/Tools/Unreal/ue.py build`.
- A reused worktree can still hold stale LFS pointers for assets that changed since its last pull. PIE tests then fail within seconds with "The summary for the package ... is invalid". Run `git lfs ls-files | grep ' - '` before testing.
- Project toolsets load only when the editor starts with `-ExecutePythonScript=<script>` that imports them; see [Register](unreal-mcp-asset-authoring.md#register). A scratch toolset with an `exec_python` tool, imported the same way, runs server-side Python in PIE; no engine tool runs arbitrary Python. Claude Code's auto mode refused to launch an editor with such a tool as a remote-code-execution surface (MST-02). Drive PIE UI with the Slate inspector instead; [Driving UI in PIE](mcp-widget-recipes.md#driving-ui-in-pie) has the recipe.
- To run a reviewed script file in the editor without such a tool, type `py "<script path>"` into the `Cmd` box (Slate inspector: `Windows` select the main window, `Snapshot` with `maxDepth` 40, the `textbox` after the `text "Cmd"` entry, then `Type` with `submit: true`). The script writes its results and a marker file that the caller waits for. It runs on the game thread and reaches PIE worlds through `EditorLevelLibrary.get_pie_worlds` (HRW-01).
  - Select the main window with `Windows` before every `Type`; otherwise the tool logs `Could not focus widget for typing` and nothing runs (HRW-04b).
  - Inside a callback registered with `unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback`, `__file__` is no longer defined; compute output paths at import.
  - Git Bash also rewrites `/GF_...` and `/Game/...` arguments of a local helper script before it builds its MCP JSON; set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`.
- `unreal.Rotator(a, b, c)` takes roll, pitch, yaw in that order. Pass keywords, `unreal.Rotator(roll=0, pitch=0, yaw=90)`; a positional yaw of -90 in the middle pitched a PIE pawn onto its back (HRW-01).
- `UWidget::SynchronizeProperties` pushes the UMG `Clipping` property onto the Slate widget. A native widget that clips in its Slate `Construct` must also default its UMG `Clipping`, or Widget Blueprints draw it unclipped (MST-02).
- The PIE window size comes from `NewWindowWidth`/`NewWindowHeight` on the `LevelEditorPlaySettings` CDO. They are not saved per user: after a restart they fall back to the engine's 1280 x 720, and only `LastSize` in `Saved/Config/WindowsEditor/EditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini` keeps the last window size (MST-10b). On this workstation they were 406 × 212, which squashes menus; set them through `ObjectTools.set_properties` before screenshots and restore them afterwards.
- The MCP server answers about 30 s after launch. Probe the endpoint, for example with `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`, instead of parsing `netstat`, whose output is localized on this machine. After a relaunch, the old log can still hold a ready line.
- An MCP client session that started before the editor has no editor tools. The endpoint still answers a small streamable-HTTP client: `initialize`, then `tools/call` with `call_tool`.
  - A Python standard-library client works (HRW-03): POST JSON-RPC with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`, keep the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header of `initialize`, send `notifications/initialized`, and send the header with every call. A reply can come as plain JSON or as server-sent events; read the last `data:` line. The tool's result is the text content, a JSON string with `returnValue`.
  - Keep each call's `arguments` in a JSON file instead of inline shell quoting; `set_properties` takes its `values` as a serialized string inside it.

## Parallel editors and ports

- Another worktree's editor may already hold port 8000. Check the `UnrealEditor.exe` command lines (`Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='UnrealEditor.exe'"`) and `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen` right before launching, and start a second editor on a free port with `-ModelContextProtocolPort=<port>`. Other sessions fall back to 8010 as well, so no port is reserved.
- A failed bind only logs `HttpListener unable to bind`, and a probe then reaches the other session's editor. Confirm `Starting MCP server on port <port>` without a bind error in your own `Saved/Logs/SurvivalRpg.log`, and never drive another session's editor.
- A port can be held by an invisible process whose PID no longer exists. Pick another port instead of using that endpoint.
- Three editors at once exhausted the 12 GB GPU, and textures rendered grey. Close editors you do not need before visual checks or cost measurements.

## Test runs

- A test editor started by `ue.py test` opens its own MCP server on port 8000 when no editor holds it. An outside MCP client then logs `Call to unknown method "server/discover"` as an error, which fails the running test. Pass `--ue-arg=-ini:EditorPerProjectUserSettings:[/Script/ModelContextProtocolEngine.ModelContextProtocolSettings]:bAutoStartServer=False` for regression runs; the same override keeps `ue.py cook` from failing on a held port.
- Stopping a background test loop does not always stop its process tree on Windows. Kill the descendants (bash, python, `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe`) and confirm that none remain.
- Do not combine `SurvivalRpg.Harvesting` with PIE network tests in one `ue.py test` call: a `Harvesting.Persistence` test leaves its `HarvestRenewableAreaTest` world referenced, and the next PIE test's `NewMap` crashes the editor with "World Memory Leaks" (HRW-01). Run them in separate calls.
- A/B against master content: `git checkout origin/master -- <asset>` runs a suite on the old asset, and `git checkout HEAD -- <asset>` inside a `trap ... EXIT` restores it.
- Importing the project toolsets writes a `__pycache__` folder under `Build/Tools/Unreal`, which `.gitignore` does not cover; delete it before committing.

## Dirty packages and modals

- Read-only inspection of graphs or component defaults can mark Blueprints dirty. Discard that with `EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.reload_packages(pkgs, unreal.ReloadPackagesInteractionMode.ASSUME_POSITIVE)`; the interactive mode opens a modal that hangs MCP. The same call drops an in-memory A/B change before measuring the saved state.
- `AssetContractTools.reload_assets` refuses dirty targets. Without Python, undo an in-memory test edit by setting the original values back with `ObjectTools.set_properties`; before closing, save the dirty packages and `git checkout` the ones that only were read or tested (MST-03c).
- Quit with `unreal.SystemLibrary.quit_editor()` after checking the dirty packages. Without Python, type `QUIT_EDITOR` into the editor's `Cmd` box ([Driving UI in PIE](mcp-widget-recipes.md#driving-ui-in-pie)); delete or save unsaved scratch assets first (MST-10a). A hard kill with dirty packages blocks the next start at the Restore Packages dialog; if that happened, rename `Saved/Autosaves/PackageRestoreData.json` before relaunching.
- `Lvl_CombatSandbox`'s enemies keep attacking while a menu is open and kill the player during UI checks; check menus and talents in `Lvl_ThirdPerson`, where the player carries the sword (MST-10b).
- Check `EditorAppToolset.IsPIERunning` before editing or compiling a Blueprint in an editor the user also uses. Compiling a CommonUI screen while PIE shows it reinstances the live widget: its graph logs "Accessed None" for every widget variable, and the action router trips the ensures `ChildToRemoveIdx != INDEX_NONE` and `RepresentedWidget.IsValid()`, which leave crash reports in `Saved/Crashes` (MST-03c).
- `StartPIE` hangs on the "Blueprints have compile errors" modal; compile the involved Blueprints and check their status first. After a folder move, restart the editor if an AnimBP reports a stale compile failure.
- `migrate_packages` opens a modal save prompt when any package is dirty, and `EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.load_map` on a plugin map path opens a blocking "Map load failed" dialog. Check the dirty lists first, and load maps with `LevelEditorSubsystem.load_level` after PIE has stopped.
- Answer a blocking dialog without stealing the user's focus: post `WM_KEYDOWN` and `WM_KEYUP` with `VK_RETURN` (the focused default button) or `WM_CLOSE` to the window titled "Message".
- After `close_clean_editor` or a user close, the process can linger with one thread and lock DLLs (LNK1104). `Stop-Process -Force` does not help; open the remaining thread with `OpenThread(0x0001)` and `TerminateThread` it.

## Assets on disk

- `EditorAssetLibrary.rename_directory`, `load_asset`, and `delete_asset` resolve a redirector to its target, so a folder move after `consolidate_assets` moved the real asset. Move folders first and consolidate afterwards, never load, move, or delete redirector paths, and delete leftover redirector files with the editor closed.
- `rename_directory` can save moved packages that still reference old paths. Save the in-memory redirectors, then `save_asset(path, False)` every moved package.
- `consolidate_assets(new, [old])` rewrites only loaded referencers.
- `EditorAssetLibrary.delete_asset` can return True and leave the file. Remove it with `git rm` after closing the editor, and stage deletions per commit, because the next commit sweeps in staged ones.
- Duplicating a map and loading the copy in the same call crashed the editor. Load the source map and call `EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_map(world, "<new path>")` instead; it writes a copy and leaves the source untouched.
- `EditDefaultsOnly` properties cannot be set on instances or placed actors (including world settings) through `set_editor_property`, `ToolsetLibrary`, ObjectTools, or the `set` console command, and a mesh's `skeleton` is read-only too. For an A/B baseline, use a temporary local C++ patch and revert it.
- Experience action sets (`URpgExperienceActionSet`) are primary assets only under `/Game/SurvivalRpg/System/Experiences/ActionSets`, as configured in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`; elsewhere the Experience manager skips them. An Experience CDO edit through `get_default_object(<Experience>_C).set_editor_property('action_sets', ...)` plus `save_asset` survives a Blueprint compile.

## PIE sessions

- Load the map explicitly with `load_level` before a scripted PIE. A PIE started as soon as MCP answers may run on the startup map with the baseline pawn; assert the pawn class in the probe log.
- Listen server with two clients: set `PlayNetMode=PIE_ListenServer`, `PlayNumberOfClients=2`, and `RunUnderOneProcess=true` on the `/Script/UnrealEd.LevelEditorPlaySettings` CDO through `unreal.ToolsetLibrary.set_object_properties`, because Python cannot see these private fields; then `StartPIE`, and restore the defaults afterwards. Without `RunUnderOneProcess`, the client starts as a separate process and `get_pie_worlds` returns only the server.
- `unreal.EditorLevelLibrary.get_pie_worlds(False)` returns the listen-server worlds, told apart by path name (`UEDPIE_n_`), and players by `get_player_name()`. Python spawn APIs reach only the editor world; spawn extra pawns in PIE with `SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(world, 'summon ' + cls.get_path_name(), pc)`.
- Multicasts sent from `exec_python` outside the world tick never reached a listen-server client. Fire them from `SystemLibrary.set_timer(actor, 'BlueprintFunction', t, False)` so they run in the server tick.
- An editor in the background throttles PIE to a few frames per second, which shifts every timer. Before timing probes, set `bThrottleCPUWhenNotForeground=False` on `/Script/UnrealEd.Default__EditorPerformanceSettings` through `ToolsetLibrary.set_object_properties`. Sample per frame with `unreal.register_slate_post_tick_callback`, and press keys with `unreal.RpgEditorPlaytestTools.set_pie_input_key(pc, key, pressed)`; MCP round trips are too slow.
- A key held through `set_pie_input_key` did not keep a `WhileInputActive` ability repeating while the editor was not the foreground application: each hold swung once, also when the press was sent again every tick (HRW-04b). For a by-eye loop, start the next activation through the ability system when the previous one ended (`try_activate_ability_by_class`), and prove the hold itself with a PIE test that calls `AbilityInputTagPressed`.
  - That holds for standalone and listen-server hosts only. In one-process listen-server PIE, `try_activate_ability_by_class` on a client world's ability system from a `register_slate_post_tick_callback` ran `ServerTryActivateAbility` locally on the client's component, which recursed through `InternalTryActivateAbility` until the editor crashed with a stack overflow; a "Deep PredictionKey Chain Detected" ensure came first (HRW-04d). Drive a client with `set_pie_input_key` on its own world's controller: press, release after about 0.1 s, and press again once its montage ended.
- The harvesting hitstop pauses the swing montage, so `montage_is_playing` reads False during it. Detect a freeze by an unchanged montage position (HRW-04d).
- With two other editors holding the GPU at 98 %, PIE ran at 3 to 4 frames per second, and swings of 0.13 s fell between frames. `r.ScreenPercentage 40` plus `slomo 0.1` or `0.2` in each PIE world gave 20 to 50 game samples per second (HRW-04e).
- A running editor keeps loaded asset files open, so a `git checkout` or copy over them fails with "Device or resource busy". For an A/B of a montage layout, change it in memory with `set_montage_clip_ranges`, leave it unsaved, and `reload_packages` it afterwards (HRW-04e).
- Another application on the GPU, such as a running game (11.8 of 12 GB, 99 % load), dropped the editor to 9 fps with "Video memory has been exhausted"; at 3 to 5 fps one frame spanned a whole tool swing and its trace missed. For by-eye checks of timing and hits, run `slomo 0.2` in the PIE world so each game step stays near 1/60 s, and capture with the Slate inspector meanwhile (HRW-04b).
- The GASP test maps spawn the player armed with sword and shield. Holster from Python with the player controller's `RpgInventoryUiActionComponent.request_clear_active_hands()`, a server RPC that runs locally on standalone authority. In a listen-server session, call it on each player's controller in the server world (`UEDPIE_0_`): the server runs the RPC directly, also for the remote client. The most recent tool pickup holds the main hand; number keys do not switch tools.
  - Tools in `Lvl_HarvestPickaxe` (HRW-01): `PickupableStatics.add_pickup_to_inventory` returns false for its world collectables. Teleport each pawn on the server 2.5 m in front of a pickup, set each local controller's `set_control_rotation` to pitch -30 in its own world, and send `F` to both controllers. After the hands were cleared, the tool lands in the main hand on host and client.
- Damage in PIE: `asc.make_outgoing_spec(GE_Damage_Instant)`, `AbilitySystemLibrary.assign_tag_set_by_caller_magnitude(spec, SetByCaller.Damage, n)`, then `apply_gameplay_effect_spec_to_self` or `apply_gameplay_effect_spec_to_target`; this drives the real death and kill-message path. `SetByCaller.StaggerDamage` breaks the stagger meter the same way. AI enemies keep their ASC on `ARpgAIPlayerState`.
  - The Python module is `unreal.AbilitySystemLibrary`, not `AbilitySystemBlueprintLibrary`, and it takes `unreal.GameplayTag` structs, not strings: build one with `tag.import_text('(TagName="SetByCaller.Damage")')`, a container with `import_text('(GameplayTags=((TagName="...")))')`.
  - A spec made from the player's ASC has the player state as instigator; resolve it to the pawn before using its location.
- Freeze an AI enemy for a probe with `stop_logic` on the `BrainComponent` (the `StateTreeAIComponent`) of its controller, then `destroy_component` its `*Driver*` components: the attack and block drivers keep attacking a player in range anyway.
  - Stop the tree only a few seconds after `StartPIE`. A stop before the tree starts is undone, and the enemy keeps chasing and attacking (CMB-07).
  - Do not `un_possess` the enemy instead: that uninitializes its ability system, and hits no longer land. Do not protect the player with `State.Evading` either: it blocks the player's attacks, as during a dodge.
- Pick up a world collectable with the interact key: stand about 2.5 m away and pitch the view down about 30 degrees until the `F Pick Up` prompt shows, then send `F` with `set_pie_input_key`. Too close, the prompt does not show. An equippable item collected while its hand is taken goes to Carry. Equip it with the player controller's `RpgInventoryUiActionComponent.request_apply_inventory_equipment_intent(inventory, intent)`, where the intent has operation `EQUIP_TO_SLOT`, a target slot, and the entry's `item_id`, `entry_id`, `placement` and `stack_count`. The `RpgInventoryManagerComponent` sits on the player state. Item instances have no Blueprint definition getter; find one by a fragment with `find_fragment_by_class`.
- The GASP test maps such as `Lvl_RpgGaspCMC` have no navmesh, so a placed AI enemy cannot walk to the players. Test enemies in `GF_Dev_Sandbox/Maps/Lvl_CombatSandbox`, which has one; after adding a `NavMeshBoundsVolume` from Python, run the `RebuildNavigation` console command before saving the map.
- A placed test actor keeps the component values it was spawned with when its Blueprint defaults change afterwards (seen with `EnemyCombatArchetypeTag`). Destroy and respawn it after editing the Blueprint.
- Never run a cheat such as `god` through `execute_console_command` with a remote client's controller in a listen-server world: the reply `ClientMessage` reaches `CastChecked<ULocalPlayer>` on the server and crashes the editor. Run it with each machine's local controller in its own world.
- Late join in one-process PIE: on the server, call `call_method('SetNetCullDistanceSquared', (small,))` on the actor; the client drops it after the relevance timeout of about 5 s, then restore the distance. The re-received actor has a new client-side name, so match it by class.
- Interaction spheres (`Interactable_OverlapDynamic`) block the WorldStatic channel, so the 120 cm spheres of stations and chests block placement footprints.

## Captures

- Never capture the whole desktop; it once captured the user's private mail window. Read the editor log, use `CaptureEditorImage`, or use `SlateInspectorToolset.SlateInspectorToolset` with `Windows` (action `list`, then `select` by index) and `Screenshot` (`ref: ""`) for a PIE client window titled `... [NetMode: Client 1]`. Capture packaged or `-game` processes with `PrintWindow` on their own window handle.
  - The `Windows` indices change whenever another window takes focus, for example after a `Type` into the editor's `Cmd` box or a Python progress popup. List and select by title right before each `Screenshot`; a stale index captured a notification window (HRW-05b).
- `CaptureViewport` renders the editor world only, also during PIE.
- A map without lights captures black, and `viewmode unlit` does not affect `CaptureViewport`. Spawn temporary lights for a shot and delete them before saving.
- Frame-exact PIE shots: `execute_console_command(pie_world, 'HighResShot 1', pc)` from a post-tick callback writes the game viewport without editor UI to `Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor/HighresScreenshot#####.png`. Its frame takes much longer; under `slomo` a per-frame sampler then measured a 60 ms hitstop as 124 ms (HRW-04d).
  - `Config/DefaultGame.ini` turns on `bDrawWeaponAttackTraces`, so swings draw trace capsules over the tool. For captures, set it to False on `/Script/SurvivalRpg.Default__RpgCombatDeveloperSettings` through `ToolsetLibrary.set_object_properties`, which changes only the running editor.
  - The third-person camera looks past the character's shoulder, which covers a contact point right in front of it. For effect A/B shots, hide the pawn with `set_actor_hidden_in_game(True)` and spawn the systems 50 cm in front of the bark; a cue point at a tree proxy can sit inside the visible trunk.
- `CaptureViewport` with a `captureTransform` renders the editor world from a fixed pose. Through the MCP endpoint it rejects a call without `annotations`; pass one with every value 0 (HRW-04c).
- A pose comparison without PIE, such as an item in the hand before and after an asset change (HRW-04c):
  - Spawn a `SkeletalMeshActor` in the editor world, call `set_update_animation_in_editor(True)` and `override_animation_data(anim, False, False, time, 0)` on its mesh, and attach the item actor to the grip socket.
  - Actors spawned with `transient=True` are missing from `get_all_level_actors`; keep their paths to destroy them.
  - Two captures of an unchanged scene already differ at edges through antialiasing and swaying foliage. Compare an after capture with two before captures, not with zero.

## Profiling

- Cost of a code path: add `TRACE_CPUPROFILER_EVENT_SCOPE`, run `Trace.File <path> cpu` and `Trace.Stop`, then export with `UnrealInsights.exe -OpenTraceFile=<trace> -AutoQuit -NoUI -ExecOnAnalysisCompleteCmd="TimingInsights.ExportTimerStatistics <csv> -threads=GameThread"` (times in seconds). Start it through PowerShell `Start-Process -ArgumentList` with escaped inner quotes; bash loses them, and nothing is written.
- Cost runs: drive scenarios from a `register_slate_post_tick_callback` state machine with `csvprofile start` and `stop` plus `Trace.File <path> cpu,frame`. Useful CSV columns are `Exclusive/GameThread/*` and `Exclusive/RenderThread/*` (sum them without `*/EventWait*` for work), `GPUTime`, `RHI/DrawCalls`, `AnimationParallelEvaluation/TotalTaskTime` for the animation worker, and `Exclusive/GameThread/Animation`; `RenderThreadTime` stays near 0 in editor PIE. CSV rows grow as stats register and the header row is at the end, so parse each row by column index.
- Euler yaw of UEFN pelvis or spine sockets is ill-conditioned; measure root yaw or lines between sockets, such as `thigh_l` to `thigh_r`.
- Blade paths and hit windows can be computed headlessly from animation data: `AnimPoseExtensions.get_anim_pose_at_time` (world space includes root motion), the skeleton's grip socket on `hand_r`, the weapon mesh's sockets (`StaticMesh.find_socket`), and the pawn's mesh relative transform.
  - A tool tip is a fixed point in `hand_r` space: compose its mesh socket, the actor's `ToolMesh` relative transform, the equipment attach transform and `Grip_OneHand_R` once, then transform it by each frame's `hand_r` pose. The same point measures clips of the animation library in a headless run there (HRW-04e). Hand speed alone hides the wrist: the pickaxe clip's hands peaked at 3.2 m/s, its tip at 7.9 m/s, and the tip reached the vein at 45 to 75 % of that peak, which read as setting the pick down.

## Packaging and separate processes

- `ue.py package <maps...>` builds, cooks, and stages Win64 Development; it took about 10 minutes and 2 GiB for the GASP maps. The staged `Windows/SurvivalRpg.exe` is only a bootstrap; start `Windows/SurvivalRpg/Binaries/Win64/SurvivalRpg.exe` to own the window and exit code.
- With `-nosteam`, the server rejects a client whose join URL lacks `?PlayerProfileId=<canonical UUID-v4>`.
- Separate-process sessions: `Build/Tools/GaspNetSession/session.py` for packaged builds that people play, and `Build/Tools/GaspPacketGap/probe_launch.py` for uncooked, scripted `-game` runs. CMC corrections show as `p.NetShowCorrections 1` log lines, Mover reconciles as `np.PrintReconciles 1` lines.
- Uncooked `-game` processes log about 58 `LogPython: Error:` lines from the engine's experimental toolset plugins; that is noise.

## Headless editor

- `UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe <project>.uproject -run=pythonscript -script=<file> -unattended -nullrhi` runs a read-only Python dump without a GPU window or an MCP port, also for another project such as the asset library.
- Git Bash rewrites `/Game/...` arguments into Windows paths. Set `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` when passing asset paths to scripts, also for `python -c` code strings that contain them; lookups otherwise fail silently.

## Rider MCP

- **Setup:** Claude Code's `.mcp.json` also configures `rider`, the JetBrains Rider MCP server. Rider 2026.2.4 answered on `http://127.0.0.1:64482/stream` and listed 91 tools on 2026-11-01. It responds only while Rider runs with its MCP server enabled (Settings, Tools, MCP Server). If Rider shows another port there, update the URL. Codex has no Rider entry yet.
- **Use it for C++ work in the solution:**
  - build state and problems: `build_solution_start`, `build_solution_state`, `get_file_problems`, `get_project_problems`;
  - symbol search and IDE refactorings: `search_symbol`, `rename_refactoring`, `safe_delete`, `extract_method`, `change_api_signature`;
  - native debugging: `xdebug_attach_to_process`, `xdebug_set_breakpoint`, `xdebug_get_stack`, `xdebug_get_frame_values`.
- **What it does not replace:** author Blueprint, Widget Blueprint, GameplayAbility and DataAsset assets through `unreal-mcp`. Build, test and cook through `ue.py`; only its verdict backs a claim that the project compiles or tests pass.
- **Its Unreal tools** (`search_assets`, `get_asset_properties`, `find_default_value_overrides`, `ue_export_blueprint_nodes`, `ue_execute_python`, `ue_play`) reach the editor that Rider's RiderLink connects to, normally the user's editor in the main checkout. Treat that editor like port 8000:
  - inspect it only with the user's consent;
  - never author assets or start PIE there;
  - never attach the debugger to it without asking, because a breakpoint freezes the whole editor.
- **RiderLink:** Rider reaches the editor only through RiderLink, an editor plugin Rider installs into the engine or the project. On 2026-11-01 it was installed in neither, and `ue_status` answered `{"connected":false}` while the user's editor ran. Tools on Rider's own index, such as `get_run_configurations` with `rootFolder` set to the project folder, answered. Prefer installing RiderLink into the engine (`Engine/Plugins/Developer/RiderLink`), so the repository stays clean.
- **Status:** beyond the tool listing, `get_run_configurations` and `ue_status`, the server is not yet exercised in this project. Record further findings here.
